rubrics.justification: Mostly consistent with a good-quality expanded blastocyst, compact ICM, cohesive TE, and thinned zona, but it over-interprets image details and introduces uncertainty/confusion around 3AA vs 4AA staging.
Integrates age, BMI, endometrium, ovarian response, first-cycle status, and male factor reasonably well, though AMH is unavailable and some interactions are discussed only generally.

Overall logic is sound, but there are internal inconsistencies in expansion-stage discussion and probability framing, with some speculative comments about sperm DNA fragmentation and grading nomenclature.

Recommendations are broadly consistent with IVF practice, including favoring single embryo transfer in a young patient with a good-quality Day 5 blastocyst; minor deviations include overemphasis on optional sperm DNA fragmentation testing.

Provides some practical suggestions such as SET, luteal support, monitoring, and considering further male-factor workup if failure occurs, but future-cycle planning remains somewhat generic and incomplete.
